recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-7084 unless a future work-group decision changes the accepted narrative CSS class set.
issue_request: FHIR-7084 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core narrative request to approve use of CSS list-style-type:none for FHIR narrative, with implementation details left to the implementation team.
initial_application: The Jira comment records svn revision 5864. Git commit 9cdb0a817b722407dfa561b2e0060ab0e4ec9873, imported from that revision, added the no-bullet list style to narrative source: source/narrative.html documented class unlist with list-style-type:none, source/basic/basic-example-narrative.xml added an unlist example, and implementations/fhir-runtime.css added a no-bullet selector under the name nolist.
additional_context: The 2015 application left a naming mismatch between unlist in the narrative page/example and nolist in the runtime stylesheet. Later Applied issue FHIR-49732 resolved that discrepancy by requiring both nolist and unlist to be defined in both places. Current source/narrative.html lists both names and explains that they are duplicates, and implementations/fhir-runtime.css defines both selectors as list-style-type:none. source/fhir.ini keeps Narrative active/normative and maps narrative/xhtml to the narrative page, so the inspected source is in build scope.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the current source already carries the requested no-bullet narrative styling support and the later compatibility clarification that preserves both class names.

related_jiras.note: Corrected the unlist/nolist naming mismatch left by the original FHIR-7084 application while preserving list-style-type:none support.
